subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX pricing & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX pricing & next steps

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and requested next steps from our call so we have alignment.

Summary from call:
- Primary pilot: conversational customer support & automated routing (two features).
- Estimated volume: 100–150M tokens/month in pilot ramp, with 300–500M tokens/month at scale depending on feature adoption.
- Key success criteria for you: predictable unit cost per feature, clear CAC payback timeline, and >50% gross margin on the product line.

Open items we agreed to validate:
1) Confirm expected monthly token ranges for pilot vs 6–12 month target (you mentioned 100–500M).
2) Target price tolerance: you said $/1M tokens is a helpful benchmark — any target range you want us to use?
3) Any internal margin targets or CAC payback goals we should model for the unit-econ sheet.

Next steps (owner & timing):
- Alex: confirm token ranges and high-level budget by end of Friday (6/19).
- Marissa/Redwood: share unit economics workbook and a couple of pricing tier options that hit your margin + payback targets.
- If numbers align, we’ll send a draft SOW and procurement link for signature.

Attaching: none yet — I’ll circulate our unit econ workbook and a tiered pricing proposal once I’ve pulled cost assumptions from SE.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX pricing & next steps

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below. Appreciate the clear recap.

1) Token volumes:
- Pilot (Q3): ~120–160M tokens/month.
- 6–12 month target: 350–500M tokens/month if adoption is strong (mainly driven by the conversational support feature).

2) Budget:
- Headline: we have a target monthly budget in the $40k–$120k range depending on final price/unit economics.
- Willingness-to-pay: for planning purposes the PM is comfortable modeling up to ~$1,000 per 1M tokens at the high end for the most performant model, and closer to $600 per 1M tokens for a mid-tier model, if SLAs and latency meet our needs.

3) Margin & CAC:
- Target gross margin for the product line: 55–65%.
- CAC payback target: 6–9 months.

Other notes: procurement will want an initial SOW + invoice terms (Net 45) and an estimate of monthly spend buckets for signature. We can fast-track procurement once we have the SOW and the pricing buckets.

If you can send a workbook that maps Redwood’s estimated inference cost per 1M tokens to proposed price tiers and resulting gross margins (plus a simple CAC/payback model), that’ll enable a quick internal review.

—
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform Product | FintechX
alex.thompson@fintechx.com | (617) 555-3498

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX pricing & next steps (internal)

Folks — forwarding Alex’s reply (below). He gave ranges for tokens (120–160M pilot, 350–500M at scale) and a willingness-to-pay ~ $600–$1,000 per 1M tokens depending on model tier. Margin target 55–65%, CAC payback 6–9 months.

Can you pull together two pricing sketches and the assumptions behind them by EOD Monday:
A) Conservative: mid-tier model priced to hit ~60% gross margin at 350M tokens/month.
B) Aggressive: high-performance model priced at the top end, prioritize latency/SLA (aim for 55% margin at 350–500M tokens).

Please use the attached workbook (unit_econ_calc.xlsx) — I’ve seeded the customer inputs (token ranges, budget, margin & CAC targets). We need:
- Redwood cost per 1M tokens estimate for both model tiers (GPU inference + infra + overhead).
- Price-per-1M suggestion for customer to hit their margin target and our commercial objectives.
- Output: per-feature cost (estimated $/monthly-active-user per feature and $/feature invocation), CAC payback table showing months-to-payback under both conservative and aggressive scenarios.

Attach unit_econ_calc.xlsx to your reply. I’ll use your numbers to draft the SOW and an initial price table for Alex.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: unit_econ_calc.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX pricing & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the quick turn. Attached is the SOW draft and a short pricing note (high-level tiers) based on the SE cost inputs. Quick summary of the pricing options we modeled (see attached workbook for details):

Tier 1 (Mid-tier model)
- Assumed cost to Redwood: $450 per 1M tokens
- Proposed customer price: $900 per 1M tokens
- Resulting gross margin: ~50–55% at 350M/month (slightly below your stated band; option priced for competitive latency/cost balance)

Tier 2 (High-perf model + SLA)
- Assumed cost to Redwood: $700 per 1M tokens (higher due to dedicated capacity & lower-latency GPUs)
- Proposed customer price: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Resulting gross margin: ~42–48% at 350–500M/month (we can tighten margin with committed volume or reserved capacity discounts)

Unit-econ outputs included in workbook:
- $/feature (monthly): we estimate $0.03–$0.12 per active user per feature depending on token usage patterns and model tier.
- CAC payback: at the proposed pricing, we model ~7–10 months for conservative scenario and ~5–7 months for aggressive adoption (assumes current LTV assumptions from FintechX).

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached SOW_draft.pdf and included a DocuSign link for procurement review: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123
2) If you’re comfortable, sign the SOW to kick off a 30-day pilot (we’ll provision capacity and finalize monitoring/SLAs).
3) If procurement wants different invoice terms (you mentioned Net 45), we can include that in the SOW.

Would you like a 30-minute call this week to walk procurement through the SOW and the pricing workbook?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

[Attachments: SOW_draft.pdf, unit_econ_calc.xlsx]
